topic: Effects of Environment on Organism Life Cycles
key_concepts: The environment includes living and non-living things.
Organisms interact with each other and with their environment to survive.
A habitat is the place where an organism makes its home.
Forests, farms, wetlands, oceans, freshwater, and deserts are examples of habitats.
The main components of a habitat are food, water, shelter, and space.
Food provides energy and nutrients needed for growth and life processes.
Water is vital for temperature regulation, nutrient uptake, waste removal, and respiration
Shelter protects organisms from predators and extreme weather.
Shelter provides space for eating, sleeping, hunting, and raising young.

Environmental changes can affect the survival and reproduction of organisms.
